verdicts.quote: To authenticate with the Systeme.io Public API, your only option right now is to attach your API key to the X-API-Key header of each request.
verdicts.reason: Vendor docs state API-key header auth as the only method, matching “API key” as primary_auth.

verdicts.quote: Click on your profile picture and select Settings… In the left menu, click MCP & API keys… You can create up to 3 API keys per account.
verdicts.reason: Keys are generated self-serve inside the account; systeme.io also offers a free plan, so developers can obtain working credentials without sales or review.

verdicts.quote: Campaigns: Create, retrieve, update, and delete entire email campaigns, as well as individual campaign steps.
verdicts.reason: The same page lists many additional resources (newsletters, funnels, price plans/coupons, courses, community, automation rules, subscriptions, webhooks, digital/physical products, offers, calendar, SMS), indicating a broad API.

verdicts.quote: The MCP server is a powerful feature included in all systeme.io plans.
verdicts.reason: Vendor markets an MCP server on its own domain, and developer docs describe “the Systeme.io MCP Server,” confirming an official server.

verdicts.quote: If you exceed the rate limit, you will receive a 429 Too Many Requests response status code.
verdicts.reason: Buildable now with self-serve keys and docs, but caveats include key-based auth (no OAuth) and documented rate limits; hence ready_with_caveats.
